reference.source: GeneReviews / Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
clinicalPearls: Caused by truncating variants in MAGEL2, a paternally expressed imprinted gene within the Prader-Willi critical region on chromosome 15q11.2
Shares features with Prader-Willi syndrome including neonatal hypotonia and early feeding difficulty, but is distinguished by prominent joint contractures
Distal arthrogryposis, particularly of the fingers, is a characteristic finding that helps separate it from classical Prader-Willi syndrome
Autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability are frequent and often more consistent than in Prader-Willi syndrome
Only paternally inherited or de novo paternal-allele variants cause disease because the maternal copy is normally silenced by imprinting
Sleep-disordered breathing, including central and obstructive apnoea, is common and warrants active screening
Some individuals develop the hyperphagia and obesity seen in Prader-Willi syndrome, but this is variable
Diagnosis is made by sequencing MAGEL2, with attention to the parent of origin of the variant
reference.pathophysiology: MAGEL2 lies within the imprinted Prader-Willi region of chromosome 15q11.2 and is expressed only from the paternally inherited allele, the maternal copy being silenced by methylation. Truncating variants on the active paternal allele abolish or reduce functional protein, which normally participates in hypothalamic development, circadian and autonomic regulation, and protein trafficking within neurones. Loss of this function disturbs hypothalamic-driven control of feeding, sleep, and endocrine signalling and contributes to abnormal neurodevelopment, while the accompanying joint contractures reflect reduced foetal movement during development. Because expression is imprinted, a variant on the maternally inherited allele is generally silent, so parent of origin critically determines whether disease results.
additionalDifferentials: Prader-Willi syndrome from deletion, maternal uniparental disomy, or imprinting defect
Distal arthrogryposis syndromes of other genetic cause
Congenital myotonic dystrophy presenting with neonatal hypotonia
Other syndromic causes of neonatal hypotonia with feeding failure
Autism spectrum disorder with intellectual disability of alternative genetic origin
additionalInvestigations: Sequencing of MAGEL2 with determination of the parental origin of any variant
Methylation analysis of the 15q11.2 region to distinguish from classical Prader-Willi syndrome
Chromosomal microarray to exclude a contiguous deletion
Sleep study to detect central or obstructive apnoea
Endocrine evaluation for hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction where clinically indicated
redFlags: Significant neonatal hypotonia with feeding failure requiring assisted nutrition
Central or obstructive sleep apnoea causing hypoxaemia
Severe contractures compromising limb function or airway
Emerging hyperphagia with rapid weight gain and its metabolic consequences
reference.prognosis: The course is variable but generally involves lifelong intellectual disability and autism-related needs; early mortality can occur in severely affected infants with respiratory or feeding compromise, whereas milder cases stabilise with supportive care, and long-term issues centre on neurodevelopment, sleep-disordered breathing, contracture management, and, in some, obesity-related complications.
pitfalls: Labelling the child as classical Prader-Willi syndrome and missing the contractures that point to MAGEL2
Assuming a normal methylation test excludes the diagnosis, since MAGEL2 sequencing is required
Overlooking the parent-of-origin rule and misjudging recurrence risk in counselling
Underestimating the burden of sleep-disordered breathing by not arranging a sleep study
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
management: Provide feeding support in infancy, including nasogastric or gastrostomy feeding for hypotonia-related feeding difficulty
Screen for and treat sleep-disordered breathing, including central and obstructive apnoea, with measures such as positive airway pressure support
Manage distal arthrogryposis and contractures with physiotherapy, splinting, and orthopaedic input
Deliver early developmental intervention and autism-focused support with speech, occupational, and behavioural therapies
Evaluate and treat hypothalamic-pituitary endocrine dysfunction where identified
Coordinate multidisciplinary care and offer genetic counselling, explaining that only paternally inherited or de novo paternal-allele variants cause disease
